subject.title: Invalid on-disk openclaw.json can brick managed gateway on next restart despite last-known-good

question: For invalid base configuration that hot reload has already rejected, should a managed Gateway restart automatically restore a validated last-known-good snapshot, or should it block the restart and require an explicit in-product recovery action?
rationale: Automatic restoration protects message availability but can revert intended configuration, whereas a restart block preserves operator intent but still requires a usable recovery surface for remote-only deployments.

options.title: Block restart and expose recovery
options.body: Preflight the persisted file, keep the current Gateway running when it is invalid, and surface an explicit Doctor or recovery action that preserves the rejected file.

options.title: Restore last-known-good automatically
options.body: Restore only a validated base-config snapshot, preserve the rejected file, notify the owner after startup, and add stale-snapshot safeguards.

options.title: Retain fail-closed startup
options.body: Keep manual Doctor recovery as the only path and document that invalid external edits must be repaired before any restart.

recommendation.title: Block restart and expose recovery
recommendation.body: Preflight the persisted file, keep the current Gateway running when it is invalid, and surface an explicit Doctor or recovery action that preserves the rejected file.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged recovery-policy work is the strongest available ownership signal for the stale-config versus availability tradeoff.
